description: Build the point-in-time event calendar from primary sources for the frozen event panel
sample: 7 event rows: IFRS 15, IFRS 9 and IFRS 16 in the EU (3), ASC 606, ASC 842 and ASU 2016-01 in the US (3), IFRS 15 in the United Kingdom (1)
outcome: 5 rows primary-verified from a directly fetched primary source; 2 rows primary-verified via the search provider's rendering of the primary page (fasb.org returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches); 1 row partially-verified with an explicit gap; 1 row unverified and marked unusable. Three date conflicts recorded; one conflict (IFRS 16 issuance, 13 vs 21 January 2016) resolved against two independent primary sources, one conflict (IFRS 9 issuance, 24 vs 25 July 2014) left open, one conflict (ASC 606 original vs deferred effective date) left open for the design to fix
key_finding: In the EU, the UK and the US there is NO reporting-framework change for IFRS 15, IFRS 9, IFRS 16, ASC 606 or ASC 842, so the frozen treatment group is empty. The only documented within-jurisdiction split in the frozen universe is the UK early-adoption cohort, which the canonical dossier has already rejected as an identification
notes: Date conflicts are recorded, never silently resolved; the date that maximises a return was never selected (D-011)

description: Assess the data route for the frozen panel: licensed route versus regulator/issuer filing route versus reduced-power open-data fallback
sample: 3 routes compared across D1-D10; price-source survivorship evidence; EDGAR timestamp documentation; IFRS Foundation jurisdiction-profile coverage
outcome: Recommended route: the regulator/issuer public-filing route as the spine, with one paid dependency (a survivorship-clean daily price subscription, roughly 50 USD per month at retail tiers). Fallback scoped to US + UK + EU-27, giving 9 independent events, below the pre-registered minimum of 12, therefore inconclusive by construction for the primary estimand
key_finding: No single route supplies both prices-with-delisted and filing-acceptance-timestamps, so a licence alone does not unblock the frozen design. An explicit authorisation request is recorded in research/data_route_assessment.md section 6.5
notes: A fallback with a survivors-only price panel biases the estimate against the hypothesis, because the firms the hypothesis predicts the effect in are the ones a survivor-filtered panel drops

description: Design audit prompted by the event calendar: can the frozen specification be executed at all?
sample: research/specification_v1.md v1.0 sections 3 and 5 against the built event calendar, and against the canonical dossier's V-009 amendments
outcome: NO. The frozen treatment group is empty across the entire frozen universe, so the frozen primary estimand is undefined. The canonical dossier independently rejects the only within-jurisdiction substitute (the UK early-adoption cohort) as an identification, forbids a group A / group B partition for a single-package IFRS adoption, requires enforcement quality and linguistic distance as mandatory controls, and records that the firm-level repeat-adopter flag is not published prospectively
key_finding: The frozen specification v1.0 must not be executed as written and must not be edited in place; a registered v1.1 of hypothesis, specification and preregistration is required before any outcome-period return is computed (D-009). No return was computed or inspected
notes: This is a design blocker, not a data blocker; no amount of data acquisition resolves it

description: Data acquisition attempt: obtain point-in-time prices, filing acceptance timestamps and as-published accounting items
outcome: Still blocked. Filing acceptance timestamps and as-published accounting items are reachable free from SEC EDGAR and the national OAMs, and the event calendar is now built; daily prices with delisted securities are not, because no licence, credential or retail subscription is authorised in this environment
key_finding: The data route is now assessed and a single route is recommended with an explicit authorisation request, so the blocker is a decision for the maintainer rather than an unknown
notes: No paid data pull was made and no new GitHub Actions run was started, per the protocol's authority limits
